newsitem.title: USA: Americans told of risk of more violence in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Americans told of risk of more violence in Israel.

text.p: The U.S. government warned Americans on Thursday that the likelihood of violence remained high in Israel and the occupied territories after Wednesday's Jerusalem bomb blast and urged them to avoid crowds.

The State Department said the U.S. embassy in Tel Aviv and consulate-general in Jerusalem "taking note of heightened tension in the area, remind all U.S. citizens that the potential for violence in the area remains high."

"Although they have not been specifically targeted for attack, U.S. citizens have been killed in past terrorist actions in Israel, the West Bank and Gaza," said a message distributed to Americans in those areas.
The warning was issued the day after two Arab suicide bombers killed 13 people in Jerusalem's main Jewish market.
Americans were "strongly advised" to avoid large crowds and political demonstrations "and not remain in an area where a demonstration or altercation appears to be developing".
